docs.title: About Me
docs.text:
I am a PhD Scholar at the Centre for Technology Alternatives for Rural Areas (C-TARA) at Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay, and part of the RuDRA (Rural Data Research Analysis) Lab. Building on my background in Civil Engineering and a PG diploma in Disaster Management with Remote Sensing & GIS from IIRS, ISRO, my work addresses agricultural water optimization for rural Maharashtra, especially for small holding farmers in this extreme times of rainfall vulnerability. My methodology centers on field-operationalizable approaches, learning from bottom up, need assessment then implement hydrological modeling rather than purely theoretical machine learning. By integrating ancient agrometeorology with multimodal satellite data (such as NISAR and Sentinel) and multi-temporal ground-truthing from inhouse built CropView v2.0 app, I utilize Python, QGIS, and Google Earth Engine to translate complex geospatial data into actionable rural applications.

docs.title: Bombay Asteroids
docs.text:
A high-octane arcade shooter with infinite procedural difficulty. Pilot your spaceship above Mumbai, dodge and destroy asteroids!

🎮 Play Now | 📂 GitHub Repo | 🌐 Live Demo

docs.title: 🚀 Overview
docs.text:
Bombay Asteroids is a fully-playable arcade game built with vanilla HTML5, Leaflet.js, and Web Audio API. The game dynamically progresses across Mumbai's landmarks (IIT Bombay, Juhu Beach, Gateway of India) as you advance through levels. Every playthrough is different, with procedurally-scaled difficulty and real-time leaderboard tracking.

Current Version: v2.3.9 (Stable)

docs.title: ✨ Features
docs.text:
• Procedural Difficulty Scaling — Asteroids spawn count grows from 3 to 16+ per level; speed increases up to 280px/s
  • Object Pooling Optimization — Efficient sprite recycling keeps performance smooth even at 10,000+ scores on low-end devices (Samsung A32, A36)
  • Dynamic Level Themes — Progress through 10 Mumbai landmarks (IIT Bombay → Gateway of India) with flavor text hints
  • Leaderboard System — Global real-time scores via Google Cloud Run backend; top 10 displayed on game over
  • Powerup System — Health pickups, time boosters, and shield protection with audio/visual feedback
  • Mobile-First Controls — Virtual joystick + fire button for tablets; keyboard + spacebar for desktop
  • Audio System — Tabla background music + procedural SFX (laser blasts, explosions, pickups)
  • Progressive Web App (PWA) — Service worker caching; plays offline
  • Responsive UI — Works on phones, tablets, and desktop browsers

docs.title: 🎮 How to Play
docs.text:
1. Enter your pilot name and click PLAY
  2. Move: Arrow keys or WASD (desktop) / Virtual joystick (mobile)
  3. Fire: Spacebar (desktop) / Fire button (mobile)
  4. Survive the timer: Each level has a countdown; reach the next level before time runs out
  5. Dodge asteroids and collect powerups:
  6. 🟢 Health — Restore 40 HP
  7. ⏱️ Time Boost — Gain 12 extra seconds
  8. 🛡️ Shield — Absorb next hit
  9. Reach higher levels → More asteroids, faster speed, harder gameplay
  10. Game Over: When health ≤ 0 or time runs out
  11. Leaderboard: Your score is saved and ranked globally

docs.title: 📊 Difficulty Progression
docs.text: Level Asteroids Speed Range Time Limit Features 1-2 3-7 50-100 px/s 52s Learning phase 3-4 9-11 100-180 px/s 40s Roll locks (drifting asteroids) 5-6 13-15 180-240 px/s 28-24s Chaos ramps up 7+ 16+ 240-280 px/s 24s- No mercy; pure reflex

docs.title: 🛠️ Tech Stack
docs.text:
• Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, vanilla JavaScript (ES6+)
  • Game Rendering: Canvas + Leaflet.js (map-based collision detection)
  • Physics: Custom arcade physics with tile-based collision detection
  • Audio: Web Audio API (procedural SFX) + HTML5 Audio (tabla music)
  • Backend: Google Cloud Run (Python Flask API for leaderboard)
  • Database: Firestore (NoSQL, real-time score tracking)
  • Deployment:
  • Streamlit (https://bombay-asteroids.streamlit.app/)
  • GitHub Pages (static version)
  • PWA (offline-capable)

docs.title: 📈 Performance
docs.text:
• Target FPS: 30 FPS on low-end mobile (A32), 60 FPS on desktop
  • Frame Time: <33ms on A32 at level 5+ (10,000+ score, 16 asteroids, 30 shots)
  • Bundle Size: ~50KB (script.js) + 600KB+ (Leaflet + Leaflet plugins)
  • Memory: Efficient object pooling prevents memory leaks at high object counts
  • Load Time: <2 seconds on 4G

docs.title: 🎯 Key Decisions & Trade-Offs
docs.text: Decision Reasoning Trade-off Leaflet.js over Babylon.js 2D-focused, smaller footprint, perfect for arcade games No 3D support Object Pooling Critical for mobile performance; reuse sprites instead of allocating new ones Complexity in object lifecycle management Procedural Audio Web Audio API for SFX saves bandwidth; no MP3 files needed Requires audio programming knowledge Service Worker + PWA Offline play + instant load times Extra caching logic to maintain Firestore for scores Real-time updates, automatic backups, scalable Requires backend infrastructure

docs.title: In the field
docs.text:
01

Open & allow

Tap “Grant Permissions & Continue” and allow camera, location and compass.

02

Start a session

Name the project. Standing? Keep the camera height at 1.5 m.

03

Wait for GPS

Stand in the open until the GPS button turns blue. Direction off? Tap the compass.

04

Aim

Tilt until the side bar shows ✓ GOOD. Crop surveys: pick the Kc stage in DATA first.

05

Capture

Hold still and tap CAPTURE. Location, look direction and tilt are saved.

06

Map

See your camera POV and ground footprint on the map.

07

Export

Before closing, open DATA, scroll down and tap EXPORT ZIP.

08

Explore

Open the ZIP in the Data Explorer, guide below.

docs.title: Capture geometry
docs.text:
Each photo is mapped as a ground footprint. Phone at chest, 28–55° from nadir reads ✓ GOOD. h: camera height · θ: tilt from nadir.

Every frame carries lat lon azimuth tilt altitude acc_h fp_w_m fp_d_m heading_source

Filename ProjectName_ID_YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_lat_lon.jpg

docs.title: Data Explorer
docs.text:
Map, browse and label your exported ZIPs in the browser. Open the Data Explorer →

01

Load ZIPs

Drop one or more exported ZIPs on the upload box. Each ZIP becomes its own colour-coded set.

02

Read the map

Click a point to see its photo and footprint. Switch layers on or off: footprint, azimuth arrow, FOV cone, capture path.

03

Colour & align

Colour points by project, azimuth, tilt, altitude or index. Arrows look off? Turn them with Rotation Offset.

04

Browse & zoom photos

Open any photo full screen. Pinch, scroll or double-tap to zoom, and drag to look around. On phones, swipe for the next photo.

05

Annotate

On the Annotate tab, select points, type a 2-digit class code and tap Apply to selected. 1st digit: crop or land type. 2nd: growth stage.

06

Export & resume

Export Annotated GeoJSON; it opens in QGIS. Import it later to pick up where you left off.

Photo viewer: ← → move · Space next · + − zoom · 0 fit · I info · Esc close

The field manual is a two-page print, with the field steps in English, हिन्दी, मराठी, தமிழ் and বাংলা.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: An interactive zoomable visualization of the electromagnetic spectrum focusing on satellite navigation and microwave bands. Explore GNSS constellations (GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou, NavIC) across L, C, Ku, and Ka bands with real-time frequency-wavelength calculations and constellation details.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
• Technologies: Interactive Visualization, Web Technologies, Geospatial, GNSS
  • Purpose: Electromagnetic spectrum education and GNSS band visualization
  • Features:
  • Interactive zoomable spectrum view (1 GHz to 40 GHz)
  • Real-time frequency-wavelength conversion
  • GNSS constellation focus cards
  • Multi-band analysis (L, C, Ku, Ka)
  • Physical size references with wavelength data
  • Auto-focus on constellation selection

docs.title: Frequency Coverage
docs.text: Covers microwave bands L through Ka, from ~1 GHz (30 cm wavelength) to ~40 GHz (7.5 mm wavelength), including all major GNSS bands used by: - GPS (NavSTAR) – United States - GLONASS – Russian Federation - Galileo – European Union - BeiDou – China - NavIC (IRNSS) – India

docs.title: Interactive Navigation
docs.text: Scroll with your mouse wheel or pinch your trackpad to zoom directly into frequency nodes. Drag to pan left or right. Click on any band or constellation card to auto-focus the spectrum view.

docs.title: Wavelength Verification
docs.text: All wavelengths calculated using $f \times \lambda = c$ (where c = 300,000 km/s): - L-band @ 1.575 GHz: λ = 19 cm - C-band @ 6 GHz: λ = 5 cm - Ku-band @ 15 GHz: λ = 2 cm - Ka-band @ 33.25 GHz: λ = 9 mm

docs.title: Physical References
docs.text: Includes spectrum allocation zones and high-density processing arrays with accurate physical size representations.

docs.title: Standards & References
docs.text:

  • IEEE 521-2002 – Standard letter designation schemas for hardware and radar-frequency allocations

13 Oct 2026 International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction

We are pleased to announce FloodView on this year's DRR Day, themed Resilience Starts at Home. In a flood, the first people to see the water are the people at home. FloodView lets them record it as data that a flood map can be checked against.

Why it's needed. Satellite flood maps come fast, but they often miss water in built-up areas, under trees and beneath clouds, and are rarely checked on the ground. Field photos exist, but they sit in phones and chat groups without position or direction. FloodView turns each one into a mapped, labelled observation.

▸ Why it matters
  • Checks the map. Points labelled flooded, waterlogged or dry show where a flood map is right and where it is wrong.
  • Marks the edge safely. The crosshair records where the water starts, so nobody has to stand in it.
  • Works when networks fail. Capture offline, keep full-size photos on the phone, and share one ZIP when the signal returns.
  • Open by default. Free and open source. GeoJSON and CSV open in QGIS, with no account or server.

A field camera for flood ground truthing. One tap saves a geo-tagged photo labelled flooded, waterlogged or dry, with its look direction, ground footprint and the exact spot under the crosshair, so you can mark the waterline from dry ground. After the flood, it records flood marks and damage.

Launch App → Explorer GitHub Sibling: CropView

Stay safe. Never wade into moving water: 15 cm of fast water can knock an adult over, and 30 cm can carry a car away. The crosshair point is there so you can tag water without standing in it.

docs.title: In the field
docs.text:
01

Open & allow

Tap “Grant Permissions & Continue” and allow camera, location and motion sensors.

02

Name the survey

Set the camera height above the ground, or above the water if you're in it, on a boat or on a bridge.

03

Wait for GPS

Stand in the open until the GPS button turns green. Direction off? Tap the compass and draw a figure-8.

04

Set the tags

Depth, flow, rising or receding, and what's flooded. They stay on until you change them.

05

Tap the class

FLOODED, WATERLOGGED or DRY: one tap saves the photo with that label.

06

Trace the edge

Switch 〰 Edge on and put the crosshair on the waterline. Walk the boundary from dry ground.

07

Fix on the spot

On the DATA tab, tap EDIT on any capture to change its class, tags, edge flag or note.

08

Export & share

Tap EXPORT ZIP, or SHARE ZIP straight to WhatsApp or Drive. Then open it in the Explorer.

docs.title: After the flood
docs.text:
Pick After flood when you start a survey. The buttons change to:

📏

Flood mark

The water line left on walls and trees. Note its height above the ground.

🏚

Damage

What is damaged (house, road, bridge, crops, embankment, well, power line…) and how bad: minor, major or destroyed.

✅

Not flooded

Places that stayed dry. Just as useful for checking a flood map.

You can also note the mud left behind and how long the water stayed. Every point gets a simple was_flooded yes/no, so during- and after-flood surveys go on one map.

docs.title: Capture geometry
docs.text:
The crosshair lands h · tan θ ahead. On the waterline, that spot is the water edge. Edge points join in capture order to trace the flood boundary. Depth on a body scale, or a measured value in cm.

The crosshair point is most reliable with the phone tilted 40–80° from straight down, the green band on the tilt bar. Each capture also stores its ± uncertainty. Look direction, tilt and footprint use the same sensor code as CropView.

Every capture carries flood_class water_depth_class water_depth_cm flow level_trend flooded_land_cover water_edge heading_deg tilt_deg_from_nadir aim_lat aim_lon aim_uncertainty_m gps_accuracy_m

In the ZIP images/ *_captures_points.geojson *_captures_footprints.geojson *_water_edge.geojson *_captures.csv

Filename Survey_FV-ID_YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_lat_lon.jpg

docs.title: Explorer
docs.text:
Map, review and export your ZIPs in the browser, on a phone or a desktop. Open the Explorer →

01

Load ZIPs

Drop one or more ZIPs on the map. Each survey gets its own colour. CropView ZIPs open too.

02

Read the map

Click a point to see its photo. Layers: footprints, crosshair points, water-edge trace, arrows, cones, walking path.

03

Colour & filter

Colour points by class, depth, flow, level trend or capture time. Hide a class, or show only edge points.

04

Browse & zoom photos

Open any photo full screen. Pinch, scroll or double-tap to zoom, and drag to look around. On phones, swipe for the next photo.

05

Review

Fix the class, depth or edge flag in the table, on the map or in the photo viewer. The original field labels stay beside your edits.

06

Export & resume

Export reviewed points, water edges or a CSV; the GeoJSON opens in QGIS. Reopen the same ZIPs later and your edits come back.

Photo viewer: ← → move · Space next · + − zoom · 0 fit · I info · Esc close

No network in the flood zone? Open the app once with internet and it then works offline. Photos are kept full-size on the phone, saved surveys can be resumed, and map tiles you've already viewed stay available. Add it to your home screen for a full-screen app.

Made by Somdeep Kundu with ❤️ at RuDRA Lab, C-TARA, IIT Bombay · Sibling of CropView · MIT License

docs.title: IBRD Debt Visualization
docs.text:
Interactive exploration of World Bank debt trajectories (1946–2025). Analyze global debt patterns with slope-weighted visualizations, regional groupings, and multi-currency support (USD / ₹ Lakh-Crore).

🌍 Explore Now | 📂 GitHub Repo | 📊 All Visualizations

📸 Click to view the interactive debt visualization screenshot

docs.title: 🎯 Overview
docs.text:
IBRD Debt Visualization is a comprehensive, touch-interactive data exploration platform for understanding World Bank lending patterns and debt dynamics across 190+ countries. The Velocity Map v3 uses slope-weighted line thickness and brightness to encode both debt magnitude and rate of change, revealing hidden economic trends.

Features interactive regional filters, country-level tooltips with INR/USD conversion, and responsive design for desktop and mobile.

docs.title: ✨ Key Features
docs.text:
• Velocity Map Visualization — Line thickness and brightness encode debt rate of change; hover for detailed country metrics
  • Multi-Currency Support — Toggle between USD and Indian Rupee formats (₹ Lakh / ₹ Crore) with auto-conversion
  • Regional Groupings — Filter by SAARC, BRICS+, G20, South Asia, Latin America, East/SE Asia
  • Time Series Exploration — Track debt evolution from 1946 to 2025 across geopolitical eras
  • Slope Analysis — Identify countries with rising debt (steep slopes) vs. declining debt (falling slopes)
  • Touch-Interactive Controls — Full interactivity on tablets and phones with optimized touch targets
  • Responsive Design — Flawless experience on 320px phones to 4K displays
  • Decimal-Precise Values — All displayed values show precise decimal places (e.g., ₹14.23 Cr, not rounded)
  • Dark Theme — Easy on the eyes for extended exploration sessions

docs.title: 📊 Visualizations Included
docs.text:
1. Interactive Timeline (1946–2025) — Explore debt trajectories across decades
  2. Time Series Chart — Track debt changes over time with line graphs
  3. Slope Interactive — Compare debt trends and rates of change between countries
  4. Velocity Map v3 — Advanced slope-weighted visualization with regional filters ⭐
  5. 20-Year Shifts Analysis — Identify how debt patterns shift over 20-year windows

docs.title: 🛠️ Tech Stack
docs.text:
• Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+)
  • Visualization: D3.js (slope encoding, interactive transitions)
  • Interactivity: Touch events, mouse hover, regional filtering
  • Data Format: Processed World Bank IBRD dataset (1946–2025)
  • Currency Conversion: Real-time USD ↔ INR with lakh/crore formatting
  • Responsive Framework: Mobile-first CSS with media queries
  • Deployment: GitHub Pages (static hosting)

docs.title: Slope Weighting
docs.text: Lines encode two dimensions simultaneously: - Thickness = Current debt magnitude (₹ Crores) - Brightness = Rate of change (₹ Cr/year) - Orange/Bright = Rising debt (inflation concern) - Dim/Faded = Falling debt (improvement)

docs.title: Regional Groupings
docs.text: Quick context switches reveal: - SAARC — South Asian trends (India, Pakistan, Bangladesh) - BRICS+ — Emerging market dynamics - G20 — Major economies at a glance - Thematic Groups — South Asia, Latin America, East/SE Asia

docs.title: Currency Flexibility
docs.text: Users toggle between: - USD — International standard, enables cross-border comparison - ₹ Lakh/Crore — Indian format for regional stakeholders - Automatically converts and formats with decimals

docs.title: 📈 Use Cases
docs.text: User Insight Policy Makers Identify debt trends by region; compare trajectory strategies Economists Analyze debt velocity; forecast future patterns Students Explore geopolitical history through economic data Researchers Export data for further statistical analysis Journalists Visualize stories behind numbers; cite specific countries

docs.title: 🎓 Data Sources
docs.text:
• World Bank IBRD Lending Data (1946–2025)
  • Dataset includes: Debt outstanding, disbursements, repayments, interest rates
  • Coverage: 190+ member countries

docs.title: 🚀 Performance
docs.text:
• Load Time: <1s (GitHub Pages CDN)
  • Responsiveness: 60 FPS on modern devices; smooth at 4G
  • Accessibility: WCAG 2.1 AA compliant; works without JavaScript (graceful degradation)
  • Mobile: Optimized for touch; viewport scaling enabled
  • Bundle Size: ~260KB (single HTML file, includes D3.js and data)

docs.title: 🔧 How to Use
docs.text:
1. Visit the visualization — Click here
  2. Explore by region — Use filter buttons (SAARC, BRICS+, etc.)
  3. Hover over lines — View detailed metrics for each country
  4. Toggle currencies — Switch between USD and ₹ formats
  5. Compare trajectories — Observe which countries' debt is rising or falling
  6. Mobile — Pinch to zoom, tap to interact

docs.title: 📱 Responsive Across Devices
docs.text: Device Width Optimized? iPhone 12 390px ✓ Touch-optimized iPad 768px ✓ Tablet layout Desktop 1920px+ ✓ Full-featured Dark Mode All ✓ Native support

docs.title: 🎨 Design Philosophy
docs.text: Simple yet powerful. The visualization prioritizes clarity—no unnecessary decorations, no chart junk. Every visual element (line, color, thickness) encodes real data. Users instantly grasp: - Which countries have the most debt (thicker lines) - Which are getting worse (brighter lines) - Which are recovering (dimmer lines)

docs.title: 📝 Notes
docs.text:
• Data extends through 2025 (latest available World Bank IBRD records)
  • All debt values are in actual currency (not indexed or adjusted)
  • Visualization updates automatically; no external APIs required
  • Works offline once loaded (no tracking or cookies)

Explore 79 years of global debt patterns. One visualization. Infinite insights.

Pujos near IIT Bombay, with a soft glow where they cluster.

বাংলায়, ডার্ক মোডে, ঠাকুর দেখার রুট সহ।

Nearest first

Distances from IIT Bombay, or from you. Directions open in Google Maps for walking or by car, with each pujo's Instagram or Facebook page where it has one.

Pandal-hopping route

The shortest walk through 4 pujos close by, drawn as a calm trail, ready to open in Google Maps.

Today, by the Bengali calendar

A slim 24-hour strip shows the tithi now and when the next begins, by the traditional Bengali panjika, with sunrise, sunset and the Bengali date. In English and বাংলা.

Know a missing pujo, a wrong pin or a pujo's Instagram page? Write to somdeepkundu@gmail.com or message me on LinkedIn or Instagram.

Bengali fonts from bangla-fonts. Alpona art by Parama Ghosh, traced from her hand-painted alponas. Dhak sound from this YouTube video.
